merger_description:
Ochre Health proposes to acquire Holdsworth House Medical Group (**HHM**) & College Street Specialists (**CSS**), NSW (the **Acquisition**).

The acquirer, Ochre Health, supports independent doctors to provide general practice medical services around Australia. Ochre Health currently operates 72 medical centres and urgent care clinics located in the ACT, NSW, Queensland, Tasmania and Victoria, but currently does not operate any medical centres or urgent care clinics in the greater Sydney metropolitan area. Ochre Health Group’s medical recruitment business, Ochre Recruitment, also works with hospitals and medical practices across Australia to source and place locum and permanent doctors across a range of specialities.

Ochre Health is majority owned and controlled by Genesis Capital, an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector.

The target businesses, HHM and CCS, are owned and operated by Rainleigh Pty Limited, in which Genesis Capital has an existing interest. HHM operates a general practice medical clinic from its premises and CSS offers administrative services to third party specialist medical service providers. Both HHM and CSS operate out of the same building in Darlinghurst, NSW.

Ochre Health and HHM both supply general practice medical services in NSW, however Ochre Health does not operate any medical centres or urgent care clinics nearby the HHM clinics. Ochre Health also does not offer administrative services to third party specialist service providers.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular, there is no overlap in the supply of general
practice medical services, or in supply of administrative services to
third party specialist medical service providers, in the local
Darlinghurst area or in the greater metropolitan Sydney area.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
